errors: No mathematical errors. The claims that each class determines its partner (F = RLP(TC), TF = RLP(C)) are correct by the Galois-connection argument.
Gap, explicitly flagged by Grothendieck: W is not yet related to C, TC, F, TF. The model-category axioms TC = C∩W and TF = F∩W, and the factorizations, are not addressed on this page.
Not stated but true: the left classes are also stable under transfinite composition and coproducts, which a small object argument would need.

ideas.what: Weakly saturated class W: isomorphisms, 2-out-of-3, and the retract condition (gf = id, fg ∈ W ⇒ f, g ∈ W)
ideas.modern_name: classe faiblement saturée (weakly saturated class of weak equivalences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs); systematized by Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs (circulated notes); taken up by Cisinski with attribution

ideas.what: Defining TF, F by RLP against generating sets C_0 ⊃ (TC)_0, then C, TC by LLP
ideas.modern_name: cofibrantly generated model structure; weak factorization systems generated by sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1967) for lifting-property definitions; cofibrantly generated framework by Kan, Dwyer–Hirschhorn–Kan, Hovey, Hirschhorn; Jeff Smith / Beke (2000) for combinatorial model categories
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses Quillen model structures and 'modelizers'; unsure whether this generating-set formulation appears there

ideas.what: Closure of right classes under composition, base change and retracts; of left classes under composition, cobase change and retracts; the Galois correspondences TC↔F and C↔TF
ideas.modern_name: basic properties of lifting classes / weak factorization systems

ideas.what: Programme of building model structures on a topos from W and generating sets
ideas.modern_name: model structures on Grothendieck toposes (Cisinski model structures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cisinski, 'Théories homotopiques dans les topos' (JPAA 2002) and Astérisque 308 (2006); J. Smith / Beke (2000)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks conjectures model structures on presheaves over test categories, with monomorphisms as cofibrations

missed.claim: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck, around 1982–83, set up a general cofibrantly generated model-structure framework on an arbitrary topos. It pairs a weakly saturated W with arbitrary generating sets (TC)_0 ⊂ C_0, not necessarily monomorphisms. This anticipates the form of Cisinski's and Smith's theorems. The mathematics itself is standard today.
missed.quote: Let moreover (TC)_0 ⊂ C_0 (⊂ Fl(𝒜)) (with no extra assumptions for the time being). We define TF ⊂ F by the right lifting property (RLP) with respect to C_0 and (TC)_0 respectively
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly a dating and attribution point for the prehistory of combinatorial model categories and Cisinski's theory. It does not contain a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Quillen lifting-property formalism and Grothendieck's known weakly-saturated condition. The mild interest is the early general setup on a topos with generating sets, written on paper dated after June 1982, anticipating Smith/Cisinski. The page contains no result beyond textbook material.
transcription_corrections: 'plus others conditions' should read 'plus other conditions we are going to list, as we need them'.
Margin note: 'NB C stands for "cofibration", TC for "trivial cofibration", F for "fibration", TF for "trivial fibration"'.
In condition b) the '[?]' after 'two of three' is unnecessary; it is the standard 2-out-of-3 condition on f, u, v.
The word inserted above 'each' under the pairs diagram is probably 'class': 'in which each class determines the other by RLP or LLP'.
The diagram's vertical marks denote inclusions: TC ⊂ C on the left and TF ⊂ F on the right (F above TF).
